clinician.final_diagnosis: an 86-year-old patient, who exhibited all the hallmark symptoms of Gerstmann syndrome, and additionally, an atypical presentation of Gerstmann syndrome in the context of a chronic subdural hematoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a 3-week history of progressive right-sided hemiparesis (MRC 3/5) and complete Gerstmann syndrome tetrad (finger agnosia, agraphia, acalculia, right-left disorientation). Admission non-contrast brain CT revealed a left frontoparietal chronic subdural hematoma (Markwalder grade 2, hypodense, 1.5 cm thickness) without mass effect, located in the dominant hemisphere parietal region. No surgical intervention was performed; instead, the patient received conservative management with Fludrocortisone. Follow-up CT on the next day demonstrated spontaneous resorption with decreased hematoma thickness. At discharge, the patient showed partial neurological improvement with hemiparesis improving to MRC 4/5, though Gerstmann syndrome features remained unchanged (neither improved nor worsened).

Hematoma located in dominant hemisphere affecting parietal lobe, anatomically consistent with Gerstmann syndrome
